media:group.media:title: Farewell, President Cabrera!
media:group.media:description:
Seven years ago, the then-incoming Georgia Tech president, Ángel Cabrera, arrived on campus on the side of the Ramblin' Wreck with the drive to advance Tech's mission statement of Progress and Service. A Georgia Tech alumnus himself, he was determined to make sure that Tech was ready for the future.
As he departs now for the Aspen Institute, we want to thank you, President Cabrera, for all you have done to make that vision a reality. Go Jackets!

entry.title: Georgia Tech Satellite Launched by NASA and SpaceX, Students Run Mission Control from Campus

media:group.media:title: Georgia Tech Satellite Launched by NASA and SpaceX, Students Run Mission Control from Campus
media:group.media:description: A satellite created at Georgia Tech is now in space after a successful launch aboard the @SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. A group of Yellow Jacket students is set to operate the @NASA spacecraft from mission control on campus. The CubeSat is testing next-generation propulsion technology during a nine-month mission.

entry.title: How Ancient Humans Tracking the Equinox Shaped Our Modern Day Calendar

media:group.media:title: How Ancient Humans Tracking the Equinox Shaped Our Modern Day Calendar
media:group.media:description: The autumnal equinox isn't a date on your calendar. Your calendar exists because of the equinox. Georgia Tech's Observatory Director Paul Sell explains how celestial motions — like the equinox — were critical to human civilization's understanding and documentation of time.

entry.title: Georgia Tech | Whatever It Is (2026 PSA)

media:group.media:title: Georgia Tech | Whatever It Is (2026 PSA)
media:group.media:description:
Whatever it is, it is never new to us.
At Georgia Tech, we’ve been applying it, questioning it, and improving it — responsibly —since 1885. Because progress starts at Tech.
The Georgia Institute of Technology is a top public research university in Atlanta, with more than 53,000 students from 146 countries. Offering degrees in engineering, computing, business, design, liberal arts, and sciences, Georgia Tech conducts over $1B in annual research that drives innovation, advances STEM education, and fuels economic growth in Georgia and beyond.
